evals.prompt: Document src/services/plan.ts. (It exports writeCounts, summarizePlan and an internal helper groupByFolder that isn't exported; the project has eslint, @typescript-eslint/parser and eslint-plugin-tsdoc installed.)
evals.expected_output: The exported functions get TSDoc comments that match their implementation, the unexported helper is skipped, only comments change, and the check passes before the commit is offered through aidevme-github.
expectations: Reads the implementation of writeCounts and summarizePlan before writing their comments
Shows a short plan (symbol, summary, tags) before editing
Adds a one-sentence present-tense summary, a @param name - description (with the hyphen) for every parameter and @returns (not @return), without JSDoc {type} annotations
Keeps the layout: summary, blank line, @remarks when needed, blank line, then the @param and @returns block
Skips groupByFolder because it isn't exported, and says so in the report
Changes only comment lines: no code, imports or formatting outside the comments
Runs node scripts/check-tsdoc.mjs src/services/plan.ts and reports the result
Offers a docs(...) commit through aidevme-github and does not run git commit

evals.prompt: Review the doc comments in src/hooks. Don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: A findings table sorted by severity, with no file edited.
expectations: Uses review mode and edits no file
Runs scripts/check-tsdoc.mjs on the hook files and counts its findings as errors
Reports a table with file, line, symbol, severity, issue and suggested fix, most severe first
Flags exported hooks without comments as warnings and comments that contradict the code as errors
Ends with the count per severity and whether the syntax check ran

evals.prompt: Fix the doc comments in src/core/format.ts. (One comment uses @return, one has @param path The path, and one says it returns null although the function returns undefined.)
evals.expected_output: The problems are listed first, fixed after confirmation as comment-only edits, and the check passes afterwards.
expectations: Lists the findings before editing and asks which to fix
Replaces @return with @returns and adds the hyphen: @param path - ...
Corrects the description to say the function returns undefined, after reading the code
Re-runs scripts/check-tsdoc.mjs and reports a clean result

evals.prompt: Add TSDoc to the components in src/components/cards/PathChip.tsx.
evals.expected_output: The component gets a behavior-focused summary and its props interface gets one comment per prop, with @defaultValue for the optional ones.
expectations: Loads references/react.md
Describes what the component shows and does, not its markup
Comments each prop on the props interface rather than on the destructured parameters
Uses @defaultValue on optional props that have a default, matching the default in the code
Says when callback props are called and with what

evals.prompt: Add doc comments to src/generated/client.ts and dist/index.d.ts.
evals.expected_output: Both files are refused as generated, with the reason, and nothing is edited.
expectations: Recognizes src/generated/ and dist/*.d.ts as generated files
Edits neither file and explains that the generator owns them
Suggests documenting the generator's input or the hand-written source instead

evals.prompt: Document the changed files. (git diff --name-only HEAD lists src/a.ts, src/b.tsx and README.md; the project has no ESLint installed.)
evals.expected_output: Only the two TypeScript files are documented; the check reports it can't run, setup is offered but nothing is installed.
expectations: Uses git diff --name-only HEAD and skips README.md as not TypeScript
Runs scripts/check-tsdoc.mjs and reports exit 2 (check unavailable: eslint, @typescript-eslint/parser, eslint-plugin-tsdoc missing)
Offers the setup from references/setup.md with the npm install command and asks before running it
Does not install any package without approval

evals.prompt: Also document the private methods of the PlanBuilder class.
evals.expected_output: Because the user asked explicitly, the private methods are documented too, following the same rules.
expectations: Documents the private methods because the user asked for them
Still reads each implementation and keeps edits comment-only
Doesn't add release tags such as @internal to application code

evals.prompt: Why does tsdoc/syntax fail with tsdoc-undefined-tag on my @note tag? Just make it pass.
evals.expected_output: The finding is explained and fixed by using a standard tag; no custom tag is added to tsdoc.json and the rule isn't turned off.
expectations: Explains that @note isn't a TSDoc tag (references/setup.md message table)
Rewrites the comment with a standard tag such as @remarks
Doesn't add @note to tsdoc.json unless the user explicitly asks for a custom tag
Doesn't disable or downgrade the tsdoc/syntax rule

evals.expected_output: The JavaScript file gets JSDoc with types in braces, never mixed with TSDoc syntax.
expectations: Loads references/jsdoc-js.md
Uses JSDoc types such as @param {string} name and bracket syntax for optional parameters
Doesn't use @typeParam or other TSDoc-only syntax in the .js file
Doesn't run scripts/check-tsdoc.mjs on the .js file

evals.prompt: I just added an optional 'compact' prop to PathChipProps and renamed its 'label' prop to 'copyLabel'. Update the docs.
evals.expected_output: Only the changed symbols in the touched file are documented: the new prop gets a comment with @defaultValue, the renamed prop's comment moves with it, unchanged comments stay, and the check runs.
expectations: Uses the After a code change flow and limits the work to the touched file and the changed props
Adds a comment for compact with @defaultValue matching the default in the code
Keeps the existing description for the renamed prop and updates any reference to the old name
Leaves comments on unchanged symbols as they are
Runs scripts/check-tsdoc.mjs on the file and says the comments belong in the same commit as the code change

evals.prompt: Add TSDoc to shortenPath(path: string, max = 48): string in src/components/shared/format.ts. (It has a one-line comment that already says it shortens the path to at most max characters.)
evals.expected_output: The existing summary is kept and @param path, @param max and @returns are added in the standard layout, even though the summary mentions them.
expectations: Keeps the existing summary sentence
Adds @param path - and @param max - descriptions, with max saying what happens when it's omitted
Adds @returns describing the shortened path
Separates the summary and the tag block with a blank line, and adds no @example since usage is obvious
